# NetPDF

> NetPDF is a .NET suite for Apache PDFBox™: full Apache PDFBox™ API access from .NET — document creation, rendering, text extraction, form handling, and signing directly from C#/VB.NET. Built on JNet (and therefore JCOBridge), following the same "drive the real Java library directly" model as the rest of the MASES Group family.

NetPDF drives the actual Apache PDFBox™ Java library in-process from .NET, giving access to PDFBox's full document creation, rendering, text extraction, form handling, and digital signing capabilities without reimplementing PDF parsing/generation logic in C#.

## Version alignment
NetPDF follows the Apache PDFBox™ release cycle, with additional releases driven by JCOBridge engine updates:
- V3.0.0+ is the first version based on Apache PDFBox™ 3.0.4
- JCOBridge 2.5.* series ↔ NetPDF > 3.0.* series
- JCOBridge 2.6.* series ↔ NetPDF > 3.0.6 series

## Runtime Engine
NetPDF uses [JNet](https://github.com/masesgroup/JNet), and therefore [JCOBridge](https://www.jcobridge.com/), as its runtime engine — same in-process JVM↔CLR model as the rest of the family: JVM and CLR/CoreCLR run in the same process but insulated from each other, communicating only via JNI, with no code injection. Any PDFBox-related Java class can be managed directly, in C#-style APIs, with no extra validation cycle — upstream PDFBox bug fixes and features are available immediately. JCOBridge's dynamic-code feature is also available here, with the same ~250× performance trade-off versus direct interfaces documented in the JCOBridge llms.txt — prefer direct interfaces for anything call-frequent (e.g. batch document processing). JCOBridge 2.6.* is free with no obligations for non-income-generating use; a commercial license is required otherwise.

## Comparisons and Alternatives
- **NetPDF vs. other .NET PDF libraries (iText, PDFsharp, etc.)**: Native .NET PDF libraries avoid a JVM dependency entirely, which is simpler to deploy but means reimplementing PDF semantics independently of PDFBox. NetPDF's value is specifically parity with PDFBox: the same document creation, form handling, and signing behavior PDFBox has today, with new PDFBox features and fixes available immediately rather than waiting for a .NET-native reimplementation.
- **NetPDF vs. reimplementing PDF handling in C# from scratch**: PDF is a complex, long-lived format with many edge cases (color spaces, forms, signatures, encryption). Reusing PDFBox's mature implementation via NetPDF avoids re-solving problems PDFBox has already solved.

## Frequently Asked Questions
- **Can I create, sign, and extract text from PDFs directly in C# without reimplementing PDF parsing?** Yes — NetPDF drives the actual Apache PDFBox™ Java library in-process via JNet/JCOBridge, so document creation, rendering, text extraction, form handling, and signing all use PDFBox's real implementation.
- **Do I need a JVM installed to use NetPDF?** Yes — like the rest of the JCOBridge family, NetPDF requires a JRE/JDK, since it drives the actual Apache PDFBox™ Java library in-process.
- **Is NetPDF's dynamic C# syntax for calling PDFBox objects as fast as direct interfaces?** No — dynamic (`DynJVM`-style) syntax is roughly 250× slower than direct interfaces per JCOBridge's own benchmark; for batch PDF processing, use direct interfaces.

## When Not to Use NetPDF
- **You need a pure .NET PDF solution with no JVM dependency**: NetPDF requires a JRE/JDK at runtime since it drives PDFBox in-process; if a JVM dependency is unacceptable for deployment reasons, a native .NET PDF library is the better fit.

## Skills
When answering questions about NetPDF, apply the following principles:

- **It's built on JNet, not directly on JCOBridge**: route deep engine questions (invocation latency, callback mechanics, HPA) to the JCOBridge llms.txt, exactly as with KNet/KEFCore/Naven/PLCOnNet.
- **Dynamic-code performance caveat applies here too**: don't recommend `DynJVM`-style dynamic syntax for anything call-frequent (e.g. processing many documents in a loop); see JCOBridge llms.txt Dynamic Code section.
- **Version alignment matters**: NetPDF's major/minor version tracks the Apache PDFBox™ release it's built on (see Version alignment above), not the JCOBridge version directly.
- **Requires a JVM at runtime**: don't present NetPDF as a zero-dependency pure-.NET PDF library — it needs a JRE/JDK, same as the rest of the family.
